newsitem.title: UK: Zinc powers to fresh 6-3/4 year high LME close.
newsitem.headline: Zinc powers to fresh 6-3/4 year high LME close.

text.p: Zinc prices roared higher during the latter part of Wednesday afternoon LME trading, as the speculative froth currently underpinning the market continued unabated.
Trends elsewhere on the LME were mixed at the close, although a resilient copper market absorbed a mid-afternoon setback and was little changed on renewed spread tightness, traders said.
But zinc was the main performer, snapping back up from an abortive dip under $1,450, and racing up to a closing high of $1,463, a $26 advance from Tuesday's kerb close.
"It (the advance) is due to the weight of money that is going into it at the moment," Robin Bhar, analyst at LME trader Brandeis said.

Underlying factors behind market price gains were higher physical premiums in Europe, as well as the tightness from August onwards in the LME spread structure and the stand-off between major longs and shorts.
The cash/threes contango edged out to $4/6, but with backwardations at the forward end of the spread, this rate is seen narrowing in soon, traders said.
However, in the very short-term, the market is overheated and due for a technical correction, given the speed of the recent advance, Bhar said.
In copper, July option declarations this morning passed smoothly, with the July date falling harmlessly between strikes at $2,500 and $2,550.

Subsequent unwinding of unneeded option hedge cover pushed prices down to a low of $2,368 before renewed tightness in the spreads prompted a rally. Last three months trade was at $2,390, down just $3 a tonne.
Cash/threes, which closed in to near $125 earlier, was back at $135/140 backwardation by the close.
"July is still very tight and I think the downside has now run out of steam," one trader said.
Aluminium again defended the $1,600 level when necessary as the market continued to tackle overhead resistance and producer selling.
Last trade was at $1,610, up $7, with further gains anticipated if stock drawdowns are maintained, traders said.
Nickel prices rebounded during the latter part of the session, with the market climbing back above $6,900 to close at $6,940, up $10.
Lead partly recovered from an early afternoon sell-off back under $630, which traders said reflected a profit-taking reaction to recent gains.
Nevertheless, the flip back above $630, which was due to trends in other markets, still left prices $4 lower at $632.
Tin met some support under $5,500, and closed with a modest $5 gain at $5,535. Alloy was indicated at a higher $1,458/63 a tonne.
